question: Under these rules, does the agency grant Jordan Ellis a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?
packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits.

question: Under these rules, does the agency grant Morgan Reyes a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?
packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)

question: Under these rules, does the agency grant Morgan Reyes a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have difficulty affording enough food in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.
text:
Caseworker note on Casey Brooks's application. Casey Brooks lost a full-time job last summer and has applied for one job in the past two months.
The household has one member: Casey Brooks (age 36).
Casey Brooks earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Casey Brooks pays $120 a month in rent and $110 a month for utilities. After rent and utilities, Casey Brooks has $250 left each month for food and all other costs.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Casey Brooks's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Casey Brooks had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Casey Brooks (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.
text:
Caseworker note on Casey Brooks's application. Casey Brooks lost a full-time job last summer and has applied for about eight jobs every week since.
The household has one member: Casey Brooks (age 36).
Casey Brooks earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Casey Brooks pays $420 a month in rent and $110 a month for utilities. Rent and utilities alone exceed Casey Brooks's income by $50 each month.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Casey Brooks's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Casey Brooks had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Casey Brooks (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have difficulty affording enough food in the determination month without SNAP benefits.
text:

Casey Brooks earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.

Before March 2026, Casey Brooks had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits.

The household has one member: Casey Brooks (age 36).
Casey Brooks earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Casey Brooks pays $820 a month in rent and $110 a month for utilities. Rent and utilities alone exceed Casey Brooks's income by $450 each month.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Casey Brooks's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Casey Brooks had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Casey Brooks (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.

question: Under these rules, does the agency deny Casey Brooks a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?
packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits.
text:

There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits.

The household has one member: Taylor Nguyen (age 32).
Taylor Nguyen earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Taylor Nguyen pays $645 a month in rent and $135 a month for utilities. Rent and utilities alone exceed Taylor Nguyen's income by $300 each month.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Taylor Nguyen's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Taylor Nguyen had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Taylor Nguyen (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.

question: Under these rules, does the agency deny Taylor Nguyen a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?
packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits.

The household has one member: Avery Coleman (age 38).
Avery Coleman earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Avery Coleman pays $130 a month in rent and $100 a month for utilities. After rent and utilities, Avery Coleman has $250 left each month for food and all other costs.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Avery Coleman's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Avery Coleman had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.

question: Under these rules, does the agency deny Avery Coleman a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?
packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)

The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

The household has one member: Avery Coleman (age 38).
Avery Coleman earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have difficulty affording enough food in the determination month without SNAP benefits.

Before March 2026, Quinn Foster had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.

question: Under these rules, does the agency deny Quinn Foster a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?
packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have difficulty affording enough food in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)

The household has one member: Jamie Ortiz (age 23).
Jamie Ortiz earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Jamie Ortiz pays $310 a month in rent and $120 a month for utilities. After rent and utilities, Jamie Ortiz has $50 left each month for food and all other costs.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Jamie Ortiz's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Jamie Ortiz had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Jamie Ortiz (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.

question: Under these rules, does the agency grant Jamie Ortiz a discretionary exemption for the determination month named in the case file?
packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have hardship in meeting basic needs such as food, housing, and utilities in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit still receives benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency grants a discretionary exemption if, and only if, in the caseworker's judgment the individual would have difficulty affording enough food in the determination month without SNAP benefits.
